title: Ordered colored-face chains and their explicit operators
statement: For a natural number $r$ and sets $X_i$ indexed by $i\in\operatorname{Fin}(r)$, a face is a finite color set $C$ together with a vertex in $X_i$ for every $i\in C$. A degree-$q$ symbol is a face with $|C|=q+1$, for $q\in\mathbf Z$. Let $J_q$ be the free integer module on these symbols, with its specified basis as in [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. A face with the wrong cardinality denotes zero in degree $q$. Deletion removes a color, replacement replaces the vertices of a specified color subset by chosen $v_i$, insertion inserts the chosen vertex at its color, and vertex maps act colorwise. The position sign is $(-1)^{|\{j\in C:j<i\}|}$. Extend alternating deletion, missing-color signed insertion, present-color identity-minus-replacement and colorwise vertex maps by integer linearity to maps $d,c_i,R_i,J(f)$. Define $P_n=R_0\circ\cdots\circ R_{n-1}$ (ignoring indices outside $\operatorname{Fin}(r)$), and $S=\sum_iP_ic_i$. The unreduced expansion recipe lists for each absent $i$ whose predecessors all belong to $C$, every subset $A$ of those predecessors, with coefficient $(-1)^{|\{j\in C:j<i\}|}(-1)^{|A|}$, insertion color $i$, and replacement set $A$. All tests use colors only, and no equality of vertices is tested.
